## Geometric sources on the gnomonic cubed sphere {#sec-ch04-gnomonic}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- The same structure as the spherical-polar source, on a grid whose two tangential directions are not orthogonal.
- Switch: none; selected by the `gnomonic-equiangle` coordinate type.
- The solid angle is exact, from a corner difference, and the radial integral is exact.
- The non-orthogonal metric adds cosine cross terms the spherical-polar source does not have.
- The cell centre is the arithmetic mid-radius, which is not the centroid of the cell measure.
:::

The cubed sphere replaces the polar singularity with six panels of an equiangular gnomonic grid. Within a panel
the two tangential coordinates are angles about two different axes, and they are not orthogonal: the metric has
an off-diagonal term, and the geometric source carries cross terms because of it.

### Derivation

The exactness of the geometry is the part worth stating. The solid angle of a cell is a difference of corner
values at `solid_angle_kj` ({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::reset >}}), which is exact for a gnomonic quadrilateral rather than
a quadrature of it, and the radial face area and volume are that solid angle times the exact radial factors at
{{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::face_area1 >}} and {{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::cell_volume >}}. Because both use
the *same* solid angle, the radial identity `[C2]` checks holds on this grid for the same reason it holds on
the spherical-polar one, and the six panels' volumes sum to the shell volume exactly, which is what the
cubed-sphere volume test asserts. A port of the corner formula confirms the exactness. The cells of a panel sum to
$4\pi/6$ for any partition, to $4\times10^{-15}$ [check `src/snapy_report/ch04/gnomonic_check.py`, output
`gnomonic_check.out`, `[C1]`]. Each cell equals the solid-angle integral over its cube-face rectangle to
$3\times10^{-15}$ (`[C2]`). Solid angle times the radial factor sums to the shell volume (`[C3]`).

The source itself is at `forward` ({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::forward >}}), with the radial part at
`src1` ({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::forward >}}) and the two tangential parts at
`src2` ({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::forward >}}). The metric coefficients they use are built once at
`x_ov_rD_kji` ({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::reset >}}). No source in the repository derives these cross terms; this
section records their form from the code and refers the geometry itself to @sec-ch03.

### Numerical method

The radial pressure force is the same plain difference of face pressures as on the spherical-polar grid, so
everything said in @sec-ch04-sphsrc about the dependence on the solver applies here unchanged.

One property deserves care. The cell centre on this grid is the arithmetic mid-radius, at
`x1v` ({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::reset >}}), and not the centroid of the cell's own $r^2$ measure. A cell average
and a value at that centre therefore differ at second order, which matters whenever initial conditions are
written as point values at the stored centre and read as cell averages. The derivation note records this as a
consistency condition on how a deck's initial state is prepared, not as an error in the grid.

The exact volume is used unconditionally. A consequence recorded in the pull request that made it so is that
the usual switch-off property does not hold on this grid: turning the related corrections off does not return
the code bitwise to the previous answer, because the volume itself changed. That is consistent with the code
and is recorded here for a reader comparing runs across that change.

### Tests

| test | asserts | tolerance |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_cubed_sphere_cell_volume.py` | six panel volumes sum to the shell volume; the radial identity per cell | `1e-12`, rest `1e-6` |
| `tests/test_hydrostatic.cpp` | a six-panel isentropic shell stays at rest over 100 steps | $\max\lvert v_1\rvert < 10^{-8}$ |
| `tests/test_coordinate.cpp` | the radial source uses the face pressure, and preserves a face-pressure gradient | `1e-8`, `1e-6` |
| this chapter's check, `gnomonic_check.py` | `[C1]`-`[C3]` the solid angle is exact and telescopes | round-off |

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The stored cell centre is the mid-radius, not the centroid of the cell measure. Initial conditions written as
  point values there are consistent with the scheme only if they are intended as cell averages.
- The exact volume is unconditional, so a run before and after that change does not agree bitwise even with the
  related corrections switched off.
:::

1. **The exact-centroid switch does nothing here.** It is defined for the radial measure of the spherical-polar
   grid and has no effect on this one.
2. **No derivation on record.** The cross terms of the source are recorded from the code only. A reader wanting
   to check them has to re-derive the gnomonic metric, which @sec-ch03 sets out.
